reasons.U1: S1 start screen explains what the AI shows and that '%는 시뮬레이션 결과이며 실제 승률 아님'; S5 help explains grades/%/lines/depth; legend always shown (AD-05, panel item 4). No explicit first-turn walkthrough, but onboarding is settled.
reasons.U2: Select-then-confirm kept for small touch targets (EV-P10); flow 4.3 covers tap/click/keyboard select, pre-confirm opponent-reply preview, swapping selection, tapping a panel candidate to select and preview its line, the confirm button, undo, and cancelling a pending AI reply.
reasons.U3: UNK-09 puts the budget to the user, and 4.2 lists what shows without scrolling at 390x844 (board with grade colors and rank numbers, confirm/undo, top candidate line), what sits below the scroll, and that no % is drawn on the board.
reasons.U4: 4.3 flow is told from the user's side: see heatmap and candidates, select, compare previewed replies, confirm, watch the ~1s auto AI reply, then the next suggestions, with branches for undo, toggle-off, timeout and off-recommendation moves.
reasons.R1: UNK-01 is top priority: it contrasts simulated self-play % (with sample size N and an 'not real win rate' label) against grades and an unfounded H-to-% conversion, notes the BRIEF conflict, and asks the user, with recommended labels in AD-12.
reasons.R2: UNK-08 sets a time budget (under 2s, single strength) for the user to decide; AD-08/09 add progressive results, a watchdog fallback and discarding late results; the flow cancels pending work on undo or new game.
reasons.R3: Eleven material decisions (win-rate meaning, product shape, AI reply mode, display toggle, mobile budget, difficulty, color) go to the user one at a time with recommendations; only local reversible details are left to the implementer (section 3).
